newsitem.title: GERMANY: "RULES OF THE GAME" PLAN FOR AIR CARGO INDUSTRY.
newsitem.headline: "RULES OF THE GAME" PLAN FOR AIR CARGO INDUSTRY.

text.p: The global air cargo industry urgently needs to agree "the rules of the game" for relationships between shippers, forwarders and airlines, organisers of the 10th International Frankfurt Air Freight Days said.

The event's joint organisers, Lufthansa Cargo AG (LCAG) and Flughafen Frankfurt Main AG (FAG), said a declaration on co-operation between the three sectors in the air cargo market would be agreed at the September 24-25 conference.

Frans Peeters, LCAG marketing manager Germany, said the draft declaration was currently being drawn up by the European Air Shippers Council (EASC) and the Confederation of German Industry (BDI) who would present it to delegates on September 25.

Peeters told an air cargo journalists' briefing that there was a growing realisation that shippers, forwarders and airlines needed to formalise their working relationships and end years of mutual distrust.
"The biggest mistake in the past was that forwarders and airlines saw each other as competitors, not partners," he said.

But the call for a new era of co-operation by Wolf-Dietrich von Helldorff, the new air cargo committee chairman of German forwarders association BSL, was a welcome sign of new times, Peeters pointed out.
Bernhard Lessmann, FAG freight logistics marketing manager, said: "The interest of both forwarders and airlines is to build up a long-term partnership."

But airports also had a vital role to play in providing reliable and attractive facilities for the air cargo industry on a long-term basis, he added. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom. Tel +44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
